lesson.child_mission: A peer feedback circle uses shared criteria (perspective control, evidence, suspense craft, punctuation effect). Useful comments are kind, specific and actionable; vague praise does not guide revision.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write two feedback notes on a sample paragraph: one weak, one strong; explain why the strong note is more useful.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: contrasts vagueness with a concrete, revisable suggestion tied to criteria.

CHECK
Only correcting spelling while ignoring craft criteria, or rewriting the peer’s whole piece in your voice.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Independently run a feedback round on your suspense draft: collect two criterion-based notes, revise one paragraph, and write a reflection naming what you changed and why.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating peer feedback on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Weak: 'It's good.' Strong: 'Your plant (rattling latch) works; delay the payoff one beat longer so the shadow lands harder.' The writer leaves with a next step.

TRY FIRST
Write two feedback notes on a sample paragraph: one weak, one strong; explain why the strong note is more useful.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: contrasts vagueness with a concrete, revisable suggestion tied to criteria.
teach_steps.explain:
A peer feedback circle uses shared criteria (perspective control, evidence, suspense craft, punctuation effect). Useful comments are kind, specific and actionable; vague praise does not guide revision.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Only correcting spelling while ignoring craft criteria, or rewriting the peer’s whole piece in your voice. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
